It reads the admin key by VALUE, not presence — a blank LIGHTTRACK_ADMIN_KEY does not change the verdict, only the diagnosis, since under Dev any/no token resolves to Principal::Dev and the key gates nothing. subject: retry-backoff
seam: crates/engine/src/retry.rs (with_retry_within: stated delay outranks the computed rung, CALL_BUDGET deadline, over-budget terminal state)
crates/engine/src/providers.rs (stated_retry_after: 3 header spellings / 2 unit systems, classified at the boundary)
crates/engine/src/lib.rs (EngineError::OverBudgetWait, RateLimited.retry_after)
crates/runner/src/compare.rs (TargetHealth: one breaker per target as a candidate filter, all-open degrades to trying)
seam_notes: The direction said with_retry's CLOSURE signature must widen so the response reaches the scheduler; it does not have to. The response is gone by then, but the CLASS is not: putting the stated delay on EngineError::RateLimited keeps classification at the boundary that holds the structured response and leaves the FnMut() -> Result<T> seam and all 4 call sites untouched. The health filter had to live in compute_cell, not beside it: compare dispatches ONE parallel_map over target x case, so a filter over a pre-computed candidate list has nothing to filter - the verdict is consulted per cell, target-major, and identity is the pre-filter index. Provider-boundary suite is a ~40-line std::net::TcpListener stub, not wiremock/httpmock/mockito: the engine client is BLOCKING reqwest and all three are async, so each would drag a tokio runtime plus a cargo-deny surface into a crate that has neither, to serve one canned response.
falsifier: The retry-after half rests on providers actually stating a delay on 429. This run could not check it - the worktree carries no engine log corpus - so it remains the proposal's own open falsifier: if a week of crates/engine logs shows no Retry-After on any 429 received, the header accept-list is dead code and only the 60s CALL_BUDGET deadline is earning its keep. The filter's falsifier is cheaper: if run history shows errored_cases at zero across every recorded run, the breaker guards a case that has not occurred.

subject: health-checks
seam: crates/api/src/health.rs:142 (live: takes no state, by construction)
crates/api/src/health.rs:147 (ready: one real store round-trip)
crates/api/src/health.rs:152 (composite: still the literal `ok`, or 503 naming the red member)
crates/api/src/main.rs:398-400 (the three routes)
crates/store/src/lib.rs:690 (Store::ping — the round-trip readiness observes)
deploy/helm/lighttrack/templates/deployment.yaml:84,92,100 (startup + liveness on /health/live, readiness on /health/ready)
seam_notes: Both probes read /health and /health was `async fn health() -> "ok"` — a constant — so readiness was a liveness probe wearing a readiness name and the pod joined the Service the moment axum bound. Split by CONSUMER, not by name: /health/live takes no AppState at all (a future edit that wants a dependency check has to add the parameter, which is the moment to remember a red there restarts the pod); /health/ready round-trips the store through a new Store::ping default (one indexed point lookup for an un-creatable project id, side-effect-free, constant on all three backends). /health stays the operator rollup and still answers exactly `ok`, which scripts/smoke.sh, deploy/README.md, deploy/cloudrun/deploy.sh and the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK all compare by string equality. Three verdicts (up/down/unknown) with a join failure classed unknown rather than down; the status code is two-state because the kubelet's question is, and the body carries the third state. A startupProbe is what makes the liveness and readiness thresholds independent, so a long first migration (the app auto-migrates on a Postgres DSN) stops competing with the wedged-process timeout — every threshold values-driven. Probe caching deliberately NOT absorbed (probe-caching governs it; nothing needs a TTL'd record at 6 probes/min). A NotReady pod is quiet, so NOTES.txt and values.yaml both say so and name what to watch — the direction's own condition for landing.
measure: false-green rate of the endpoint the chart's readinessProbe reads, over one probe window (8 probes) against a real SqliteStore severed mid-test, with the pre-split handler reproduced verbatim so the before number is observed rather than remembered (crates/api/src/tests_health.rs): 8/8 green -> 0/8. Liveness on the same severed store: 8/8 green after (no restart for a dependency failure), which is the mirror-image defect the split also has to avoid. Writes routed to that instance while the old probe was green: 8/8 served as 5xx.

If /health ever becomes a cost surface that matters, the answer is a TTL'd record per probe-caching, NOT a boot-time flag. Second falsifier still open: the restart-count number is structural here, not measured on a cluster — nobody has installed this chart against a slow Postgres and counted container restarts, so 'restarts caused by a healthy-but-slow dependency: 0' remains predicted rather than observed.

subject: error-handling
seam: crates/core/src/event.rs:132 (FailureClass: transient | terminal | unknown, from_wire quarantines the rest)
crates/core/src/event.rs:301 (LlmEvent::failure_class — typed accessor, never inferred from `error`)

crates/responder/src/pipeline.rs:57 (the wired decision + the per-branch counters)
seam_notes: The class is carried in metadata.failure_class rather than as a new column — the same choice, for the same stated reason, as customer_id / cost_source / api_key_id: metadata rides unchanged through SQLite, Postgres and Firestore, so this needed no migration in three backends and no conformance change. It is still a structured, closed-vocabulary field validated at the boundary and read through a typed accessor, which is what the corpus rule requires of a classifier input; the responder matches on a FailureClass variant, not on prose. Added to redact.rs's METADATA_PASSTHROUGH (5 -> 6) because scrubbing it would send every failure downstream as though its producer had said nothing — exactly the state it exists to distinguish from. The third state earns its place BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by assertion: `terminal` goes to investigation WITHOUT consulting the message, `unknown` is the only input that reaches classify() at all, so the direction's 'two states by another door' failure is unreachable here. crates/responder gained a lighttrack-core dependency for FailureClass alone, so the vocabulary has one address. The phrase list is not deleted and is not the defect: it is the correct handling for a producer that said nothing, and every use of it is now counted (GET /classification on the responder, fallback_rate). Deliberately not absorbed: EngineError's taxonomy, breaker.rs's admission control, the Determinism marker, personas' AppError.
measure: classifier disagreement over a 20-row corpus of real provider/application failure shapes (Anthropic + OpenAI SDKs, litellm, httpx, gRPC, psycopg, plus the app errors around them), each row carrying the class an SDK holding the response would have minted (crates/responder/src/classify.rs): reading the message reaches a different verdict on 8 of 20 rows -> the carried class is wrong on 0 of 20. Five of the eight are provider transients the phrase list misses (a paid investigation against a codebase with no bug in it); three are terminal bugs whose text contains a transient phrase ("timed out waiting for the retry mock") and are therefore skipped and never diagnosed. Decisions made by reading prose (fallback_rate): 1.0 -> 0.0 for a producer that mints the class.

subject: federated-benchmark-sharing
seam: crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:271 (build_digest filtered thin buckets and returned only survivors — the withheld count was computed nowhere)
crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs (new: build_digest_counted returns (entries, withheld); build_digest delegates so no caller moved)
crates/core/src/collective/types.rs:113 (CollectiveDigest.buckets_withheld, serde-defaulted like the consent fields)
crates/api/src/collective/digest.rs:58 (build_instance_digest populates it)
crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs tests (2 new: the disclosure arms, and the hash-stability pin)
seam_notes: The floor's enforcement half was correct and its disclosure half was absent, while the consent envelope beside it (projects_included/projects_excluded) was disclosed properly — which is what makes this an oversight rather than a decision. The load-bearing choice is what the count is NOT part of: digest_sha256 hashes an explicit field list, not the struct, and the contribution ledger gates repeat pushes on it. Adding buckets_withheld to the hash would have been defensible (it is a real difference between two observations) and would have made every existing instance re-push unchanged data once; it was left out because the hash gates whether a push carries new EVIDENCE, and two digests with identical entries carry the same evidence however many thin buckets sat behind them. A test pins that so a later change cannot quietly reintroduce the re-push. Deliberately not touched: the floor value itself, the source floor at the hub, and the merge path.
measure: whether an operator previewing the digest can distinguish 'held back by the floor' from 'nobody measured this'. Arm A (before): one 3-case bucket at floor 5 and an empty store both yield entries:[] with no other output — the two states are byte-identical. Arm B (after): the same two inputs yield buckets_withheld 1 and 0. Mixed case (one 6-case, one 2-case, floor 5) yields entries:[1] + withheld:1, confirming the count reports suppression rather than bucket totals. Distinguishable states: 0 of 2 -> 2 of 2.
gate: cargo test -p lighttrack-core --lib 253 ok (+2 new); cargo test --workspace green across all 20 suites, none moved
falsifier: The hash decision is the one that could be wrong, and it is stated rather than proven: if a hub ever wants to distinguish two contributions whose entries match but whose suppression differed, the count would have to enter the hash and every instance would re-push once. Nothing in the tree needs that today. Also undischarged: no surface renders buckets_withheld yet — the field is on the API response and the CLI/UI do not show it, so an operator gets the distinction only by reading the JSON. That is the next piece, not done here.
